source: UCS only (hyperswitch-prism). Scored from Rust source; the field probe is a secondary signal.

capabilities.label: MIT
capabilities.description: Merchant-initiated charge against a stored mandate.

capabilities.label: $0 Auth
capabilities.description: Zero-amount authorization that stores a mandate.

capabilities.label: Webhooks (payments + refunds)
capabilities.description: Incoming webhook handling: the connector overrides the inert IncomingWebhook defaults.

capabilities.label: NTID support for MIT
capabilities.description: Consumes a network transaction id to authorize a merchant-initiated transaction.

capabilities.label: Chargeback proof submission
capabilities.description: Submits dispute evidence to the processor.

capabilities.label: 3DS (native)
capabilities.description: Native 3D Secure inside the connector's own Authorize flow. NO SINGLE CERTAIN SIGNAL EXISTS: connectors express it three different ways (stripe maps AuthenticationType::ThreeDs to a request value, checkout uses a force_3ds field, adyen an enum), and is_three_ds() is equally the guard used to REJECT 3DS. Ranked by evidence strength; connectors emitting only a generic redirect stay unknown.

capabilities.label: Auto capture
capabilities.description: Authorize-and-capture in one call. UCS defaults CaptureMethod to Automatic, so this is the ABSENCE of an explicit refusal rather than a positive confirmation — read a high count as 'not refused', not as 'verified'.

capabilities.label: Decrypted wallet, HS creds
capabilities.description: Apple Pay / Google Pay decrypted with Hyperswitch-held certificates. Detected from the decrypted-token types the connector consumes. Payment-method parsing is unreliable in general (a naive pass classified stripe as not supporting Card), so this is indicative, not proven.
